---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pizlonator/fil-c (pizlonator/fil-c)</summary>

### [`v0.677`](https://redirect.github.com/pizlonator/fil-c/releases/tag/v0.677): Fil-C Linux/x86_64 version 0.677

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pizlonator/fil-c/compare/v0.676...v0.677)

This is a bugfix release.

- Makes `prctl` calls for installing sandboxes apply to Fil-C runtime threads as well as the calling thread.
- Harden the implementation of `fork(2)` against signals even in cases where the libc gets it wrong.
- Support more long double math functions in glibc.
- Improve the compiler's use of linker attributes. Results in a small improvement to code size of stripped binaries.
- Make sure that `SIGSYS` cannot be handled.
- Fix a super rare GC crash resulting from a race condition in libpas's medium size lookup table.

Guide to the available files:

- `filc-0.677-linux-x86_64.tar.xz` is the traditional, self-contained ["pizfix"](https://fil-c.org/pizfix) distribution. It only includes the compiler, doesn't require root, and is based on the musl libc. This is recommended for quickly trying out Fil-C.
- `optfil-0.677-linux-x86_64.tar.xz` is the [/opt/fil](https://fil-c.org/optfil) distribution. It includes many useful programs like OpenSSH, sudo, tmux, and git. It's based on glibc 2.40, and requires root permissions. This is recommended for giving Fil-C deeper scrutiny.

</details>
